items.heading: Resolution Rescinding Berkeley Police Department’s Pepper Spray Reporting Requirement (Reviewed by the Public Safety Committee)
items.action: Action: M/S/C (Lunaparra/Tregub) to suspend the rules and extend the meeting to 11:20pm. Vote: All Ayes. Action: 24 speakers. M/S/C (Ishii/Kesarwani) to adopt Resolution No. 72,159–N.S. as proposed by Mayor Ishii in Supplemental Communications Packet #2 and further amended at the meeting to read as below. RESOLUTION RESCINDING THE PEPPER SPRAY INCIDENT NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENT WHEREAS, in 1997 the City Council established a requirement for the Berkeley Police Department to notify Council each time pepper spray is used as a measure to bolster accountability; and WHEREAS, the separate notification process was introduced at a time when reporting mechanisms were limited and provided necessary oversight; and WHEREAS, the Berkeley Police Department has since implemented a comprehensive use- of-force reporting system that documents all related incidents, including those involving pepper spray in the Transparency Hub and the annual Use of Force report; and WHEREAS, until February 10, 2026, the Berkeley Police Department historically included pepper spray in the annual Controlled Equipment report; and WHEREAS, the Police Accountability Board submitted a recommendation to the City Council on February 23, 2026 that recommended reincorporating reporting on the use of pepper spray into the annual Controlled Equipment report to preserve key narrative details not otherwise available through BPD’s other reporting channels; and WHEREAS, the administration of first aid was included in the original pepper spray use report that was transmitted to the Mayor and Council within 7 days; and WHEREAS, the continued requirement for separate notification directly to the Mayor and City Council creates redundant administrative tasks that strain City resources; and WHEREAS, rescinding the notification requirement will simplify reporting procedures and allow staff to concentrate on more critical operational matters while preserving public transparency. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City Council of the City of Berkeley that: 1. The requirement for the Berkeley Police Department to notify the City Council every time pepper spray is used is hereby rescinded. 2. All pepper spray incidents shall be recorded as part of the established use-of-force reporting system in accordance with current departmental protocols. 3. Subsequent to the pepper spray report being signed off on by the Police Department chain of command, no later than 14 days after the use of the chemical agent, all pepper spray incidents shall be recorded on the Transparency Hub, including information about: a. The incident itself, including time, date, location where the incident occurred and level of use of force; and b. The suspect themselves, including age, race, sex, subject altered state, and use of force reason; and c. The officer role; and d. Enhance the definitions for the various Use of Force levels and clearly identify pepper spray use as Level 3; e. Include clear navigational guidelines so users can more easily access the open data portal and seek information on chemical agent use. 4. Refer to the City Manager to present an amendment to BMC Chapter 2.100 to the City Council to subject pepper spray to the approval and reporting requirements of the Controlled Equipment Ordinance, including the administration of first aid. Work with the vendor to determine if reporting the administration of first aid, a narrative report, and opt-in notifications are possible to include in the Transparency Hub. Vote: All Ayes.
